blocks.text: Indian dance forms can be divided into two types:
1. Classical Dance Forms: They have particular steps that need to be performed in particular events (mostly performed in temples).
2. Folk Dance Forms: No particular steps are defined. They are performed in a specific ritual.
There are 8 classical dances according to Sangeet Natak Academi (HQ: New Delhi) however the Ministry of Culture recognises 9 classical dances (8 classical dances + Chhau).
Origin: Rooted in Natya Shastra (considered as "Fifth Veda"), written by Bharat Muni.
Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikeshvara describe expres- sions, movements, and gestures.
Nritta: Purest form of dance.
Nritya: Expressive form of dance (pure dance + expression).
It is the oldest classical dance of India that is performed solo (by a single person) + known as Ekaharya.
Earlier Names: Sadirattam, Thevarattam, Parathaiyar Attam.
Bharatnatyam was earlier also known as Dasiattam as it was traditionally performed by Devadasis (female dancers)
in temples (last surviving devadasi: R. Muthukannammall).
It is found in Natya Shastra and is associated with Kalakshetra style.
It was banned by Britishers in 1910 but was later revived.
Revival by: E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale — renamed the dance Sadirattam to Bharatnatyam.
Forms of Classical Dance:
Shaivite (majority)— Dedicated to Lord Shiva (masculine).
Vaishnavite — Dedicated to Lord
References in literature: Found in Cilappatikaram (by Tlango Adigal) and Manimegalai (by Chithalai Chathanar).
Main mudra: Kataka Mukha Hasta Bharatnatyam was performed by certain families of the Tanjore district and these inheritors were known as 'Nattuvanar'.
Performance Style: Pandanallur, Vazhuvoor, Kalakshetra, Melattur, Tanjore
Movements/Stages of Dance: Alarippu (flowers offering), Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana, Mangalam.
Tamil text Tolkappiyam was composed during 2nd Sangam.
Tandava: Masculine (Shiva)
Bharatnatyam is also depicted in temple Gopuram (Chidambaram Temple).

Earlier known as: Bhagavata Mela Dance (Tanjore, Tamil Nadu).
Modern form of dance is attributed to: Tirtha Narayan- ayati and Siddhendra Yogi (developed as a dance-drama — Bhama Kalpam (story of Satyabhama, the charming but jealous wife of Lord Krishna)}
Elements: Ganesha Vandana, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Kalapam, Padam, Tarangam (it is the concluding part of dance where the dancer dances on a rim of brass plate).
Yakshagana was performed in Andhra Pradesh in earlier times. It is traditionally performed from dusk till dawn.
